definition: Planning by simulating many futures from the current state, expanding a search tree guided by value estimates (the heart of AlphaGo).
details: Planning by simulating many futures from the current state, expanding a search tree guided by value estimates (the heart of AlphaGo). Its ideas reappear in LLM test-time search over reasoning paths.

explainer.lead: Monte Carlo Tree Search plans by simulating many futures from the current state and expanding a search tree guided by value estimates. It matters because it made strong play possible in games like Go as the heart of AlphaGo.

tiers.eli5: It is like trying many possible moves in your head, keeping track of which ones looked promising, before choosing one.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for planning in games and, increasingly, for searching over candidate reasoning paths at LLM inference time. A pitfall is that simulation cost grows with the number of futures explored, so budget and value estimates must be tuned carefully.
tiers.paperLevel: A planning method that builds a search tree by simulating many futures from the current state, expanding the tree guided by value estimates. Its known limits are the cost of running many simulations and the reliance on the quality of value estimates.

explainer.example: AlphaGo uses Monte Carlo Tree Search as its heart, simulating futures and expanding the tree under value estimates during play.
